title: Custom properties (CSS variables)
learningObjectives: Explain custom properties (css variables) and apply the concept in maintainable CSS.

understand.concept: CSS custom properties are declared with names beginning with two hyphens, usually on a selector, and consumed with var(). They participate in the cascade and inherit by default. They can hold reusable design values such as colours, spacing, and component settings.
understand.whyItMatters: Custom properties reduce duplicated values and make theme changes easier. Because they inherit and cascade, scope them intentionally and consider where a component should receive its tokens.
understand.analogy: A custom property is a named design token that can be reused wherever its value is needed.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual cascade, inheritance, and rendering follow CSS specifications.

explain.narrative: The brand colour and spacing are defined once and reused in the card.

practise.guidedTask: Create root-level colour and spacing tokens, then override one token on a themed component.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component or page section that uses the concept. Test alternate content and, where relevant, right-to-left direction or reduced-motion settings.

questions.answer: With names beginning with two hyphens

questions.prompt: What is a maintainable way to use CSS features across a project?
options: Use clear reusable rules and test computed behaviour
Copy unrelated declarations into every component
Ignore writing direction and user preferences
questions.answer: Use clear reusable rules and test computed behaviour
questions.explanation: Reusable CSS should remain understandable and work across relevant content and user settings.
